svg.text: Batching: which tokens run together in one step
Toy example: 5 requests, 3 batch slots · one column = one engine step · prefill of new requests not shown
output tokens: A=3 B=7 C=4 D=5 E=2 prompt lengths (panel 2): A=5 B=2 C=3
Static or continuous: when can a new request join?
Static batching waits for the whole batch to finish. Continuous batching refills a slot at the next step.
Batch 2 (D, E) starts after B ends at step 7.
D takes A's slot at step 4; E takes C's slot at step 5.
Dashed cell = an idle slot: the device does no useful work there.
Padded or packed: how is the batch stored?
A padded batch fills every row to the longest prompt. A packed (varlen) batch puts the tokens end to end.
cu_seqlens_q = [0, 5, 7, 10] → sequence i owns tokens cu[i] … cu[i+1] − 1
10 slots, 0 padding. Kernels read the boundaries from cu_seqlens_q.
In DeepInfer, one step is a prefill step or a decode step
The NORMAL engine does not mix the two kinds in one step. Both kinds use a packed batch.
Prefill step · token budget max_num_batched_tokens (4,096 here, illustrative)
The rest of P3 (1,904 tokens) waits for a later prefill step. In a NORMAL engine, a chunked prompt ends the step.
Decode step · every running sequence sends 1 token + 5 draft tokens (DEEPINFER_USE_NEXTN_DECODE = 5)
One colour = one request. Dashed box = a prompt chunk (panel 3, top) or a draft token d1-d5 (panel 3, bottom).
Simplified: a joining request first needs a prefill step. Panel 1 leaves it out, so the grid shows decode work only.
